findings.title: [P1] Keep the branch argument out of the shell
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell syntax, such as `main; arbitrary-command`, `exec` interprets it as part of the command and executes it with the application's privileges. The previous `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` implementation passed the value as a literal argument. Retain an argument-array API instead of interpolating `branch` into a shell command.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve cancellation of the Git process
findings.body:
`exec()` returns the shell process rather than `git`. On Windows, calling `.kill()` on the returned child terminates `cmd.exe` but can leave its `git show` child running. Cancellation during a large or slow `git show` therefore leaks work and may keep inherited output handles open.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Keep the branch argument out of the shell
findings.body:
`exec()` interpolates `branch` into a shell command, enabling arbitrary command execution. For example, `showBranch("HEAD; touch /tmp/pwned")` runs both commands whenever caller-controlled input reaches this exported API. The previous `execFile()` call passed the branch as a literal argument.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore argument-safe Git invocation
findings.body:
`exec` passes the interpolated branch through a shell. A branch value such as `main; touch /tmp/pwned` or `$(malicious-command)` executes arbitrary commands with the application’s privileges whenever callers provide untrusted branch input. The previous `execFile` argument array did not interpret shell metacharacters.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
